claims.text: Under the ordinary retryable-writes specification, updateMany() and deleteMany() are unsupported because one statement can affect multiple documents; Percona also describes this multi-document restriction. (high confidence)

Inside a transaction, the retryable-writes specification supports only commitTransaction and abortTransaction as retryable write commands. Other writes must not be retried or receive a driver-added RetryableWriteError label even when retryWrites is true. (low confidence)

For MongoDB 4.4 and newer, the retryable-writes specification delegates server-response RetryableWriteError labeling to the server; drivers must not add this label to a non-network error derived from that server response. (low confidence)

The CSOT specification defines timeoutMS as a best-effort maximum and requires documented exceptions for blocking sections that the driver cannot fully control; its example is OCSP verification exceeding the operation timeout. (low confidence)

The CSOT specification requires a distinguishable timeout error, while retryable-writes pseudocode throws `previousError` when `timeoutMS` expires. DRIVERS-3385 explicitly identifies this contradiction; the evidence does not establish one universal driver error shape. (high confidence)

The retryable-writes specification stops retries on success or a non-retryable error; without CSOT it permits one retry, while with CSOT retries continue within the operation timeout. The CSOT specification likewise limits repeated retries by timeout expiration or a non-retryable error. (high confidence)

Under CSOT, server selection uses `min(serverSelectionTimeoutMS, remaining timeoutMS)`. Connection checkout uses what remains of that computed timeout, so the configured operation budget does not replace the server-selection limit unconditionally. These minima use the specification’s convention: when 0 means infinite, min(0, other) evaluates to other. (low confidence)

Under the client-backpressure specification, encountering an overload error caps subsequent retries under any retry policy at `MAX_RETRIES`, including retries for errors that are not overload errors. This qualifies the ordinary CSOT rule of retrying within the remaining budget. (high confidence)
The CSOT specification applies timeoutMS to the whole multi-batch operation, rather than granting a fresh timeout to each batch. (low confidence)

The CSOT specification defines `timeoutMS` as a best-effort operation limit. For a batched operation, the budget applies to the entire operation rather than restarting for each batch. (low confidence)

For collection-level and client-level bulkWrite(), the retryable-writes specification evaluates each command after order and batch splitting. A batch containing UpdateMany or DeleteMany is ineligible; drivers must not change splitting to maximize retryability. (low confidence)
The retryable-writes specification excludes unacknowledged writes, including {w: 0}; drivers must neither add a transaction ID nor retry these commands. (low confidence)

With retryWrites enabled, the retryable-writes specification requires drivers to add RetryableWriteError to network errors establishing an initial connection, network errors communicating with a supporting server, and PoolClearedError during connection checkout in a CMAP-compliant driver. (low confidence)

The Node.js driver 6.11.0 release notes introduced CSOT as experimental and listed CSOT support for retryable reads and writes. Those notes document that timeoutMS overrides socketTimeoutMS, waitQueueTimeoutMS, wTimeoutMS, maxTimeMS, and maxCommitTimeMS, while serverSelectionTimeoutMS is not unconditionally overridden. (low confidence)

The accepted client-backpressure specification defines a separate overload policy that can retry updateMany and other commands excluded by ordinary retryable-write rules. It requires both SystemOverloadedError and RetryableError labels; its default MAX_RETRIES is 2, configurable through maxAdaptiveRetries, and a CSOT retry also needs remaining time. This is a specification statement. (low confidence)
DRIVERS-3385 is closed with resolution Won’t Fix, and its resolved timestamp is October 31, 2026. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)
The retryable-writes specification defines `retryWrites` as a client-level boolean that defaults to true; it must not be configured per database, collection, or individual write. (low confidence)

Server eligibility requires session support, detected through `logicalSessionTimeoutMinutes` in the handshake response, and a server type other than standalone. If the initially selected server lacks support, the driver executes without a transaction ID and does not retry. (low confidence)

Supported operations include `insertOne`, `updateOne`, `replaceOne`, `deleteOne`, `findOneAndDelete`, `findOneAndReplace`, `findOneAndUpdate`, `insertMany`, and eligible `bulkWrite` batches. The driver evaluates each resulting command after order and batch splitting, without changing splitting to maximize retryability. (low confidence)

Ordinary retryable writes exclude aggregation write stages such as `$out` and `$merge`. Within transactions, only `commitTransaction` and `abortTransaction` qualify; individual writes must not be retried or given the `RetryableWriteError` label. (low confidence)

The driver treats the `RetryableWriteError` label as retryable. With `retryWrites` enabled it adds the label to network errors and `PoolClearedError` during checkout. For server versions 4.4 and newer, the server classifies server-response errors; the driver must not add the label to those response errors. (low confidence)

The Node.js driver 6.11.0 release notes introduce CSOT as experimental and advise against production use until stable. The same release notes exclude implicit initial connection work from the configured `timeoutMS` bound and recommend explicitly connecting before operations using CSOT. These statements concern that historical release. (low confidence)
